🏬 Shoe Store & CalSims Consumer Market

The Shoe Store is an independent retailer. CalSims is a separate aggregate consumer economy that can buy goods from this and future businesses. CalSims is not a company and has no stock or public valuation.

CalSims Consumer Cash$5,000M
Spendable Cash$4,000M
Protected Reserve$1,000M
Shoe Store Cash$0M

CalSims begins with a $5B consumer pool: $4B is initially spendable and $1B is protected. Spending is demand-driven, not a target. Shoe prices are chosen by each company; there are no preset retail prices.

Release a Shoe Model

Choose a player currently signed to the selected shoe company.

Development cost and any selected boost fee are paid upfront by the shoe company. Each company gets one boost attempt per season. Fees are not refunded if a boost fails. A successful boost adds 20 popularity points for two seasons.

Automatic Consumer Sales

CalSims automatically simulates consumer shoe purchases after each completed game. Demand is shared among active models according to price and popularity; consumers may skip buying. Sales are capped by CalSims' spendable cash. Each completed game is processed once, even if the app is refreshed.

Automatic sales will be processed after the next completed game.

Investor Purchase

Eligible citizens, businesses, and teams may purchase from an open offering using available cash. Federal Reserve and CalSims accounts are not investors.

Maturity Processing

Due securities are repaid manually. Processing is blocked if the Federal Reserve lacks the cash needed to pay all due principal and interest. Each security can mature only once.

Accounting: purchases transfer existing cash from investor to Federal Reserve and create a matching principal liability. Interest is calculated as principal × per-season rate × term. No money is created at issuance. Maturity repayment reduces Federal Reserve cash and clears the liability.

ℹ️ Basketball Information

Season Rules

  1. Each team plays every other team once.
  2. Best record normally receives the championship bye.
  3. If tied for best record, the defending champion gets the bye when involved.
  4. If all three tie, the previous champion gets the bye.
  5. Season 29 starts from the permanent Season 28 championship record; Season 28 champion Dunks enters as defending champion.
  6. The other two teams play the semifinal.
  7. Semifinal winner plays the bye team for the championship.
  8. The team receiving the playoff bye gets $60M.
  9. Champion receives $100M; runner-up receives $50M.

Game Rules

  • Each player gets two point dice and two rebound dice per quarter.
  • There are four quarters.
  • Overtime uses one point die and one rebound die per player until the tie is broken.

Ticket Revenue

Every game gets two dice. Each die is worth $10M. Total range: $20M–$120M.

Ticket revenue is split 70% to the winner and 30% to the loser.

Shoe Revenue

Each shoe company gets two dice rolls per game ($20M–$120M) when it has an active player deal. TV Company also rolls two dice ($20M–$120M) and receives an additional 10% of total shoe-company revenue. The TV share does not reduce shoe-company revenue.

🏢 Business Ownership Marketplace

Buy and sell ownership stakes directly between citizens. Prices are calculated from the business valuation. A resale never changes the business's cash balance.

Sports Bets Company Debt

Sports Bets Company can issue debt to raise cash. Citizens and businesses may buy portions of an issuance; basketball teams and Sports Bets Company itself cannot buy. At payoff, each holder receives principal plus a one-time 0.25% interest payment on the principal they purchased. The debt register tracks each owner, ownership percentage, principal, interest and payout.

Issue Debt Features
